You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

Prepare the first assessment of the original records for a possible handoff.

{"scenario":"Birchwood wayfinding","question":"Can the clerk mark installation complete for the northern signs?","claims":{"A":"The signs were mounted facing the paths on opening day.","B":"The signs were made of wood.","C":"The signs were delivered on Thursday."},"sources":{"S1":"signed carrier slip records Thursday delivery.","S2":"inventory lists four aluminium signs.","S3":"the foreman's work order describes the intended orientation and was checked off without requiring an orientation photograph."}}

message.content: {"claims":{"A":{"status":"unresolved","citations":[],"confidence":40},"B":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["S2"],"confidence":10},"C":{"status":"supported","citations":["S1"],"confidence":90}},"note":"Claim C is supported by the signed carrier slip in S1 confirming Thursday delivery. Claim B is contradicted by S2, which lists four aluminium signs, indicating the signs were not made of wood. Claim A is unresolved; while S3 describes intended orientation and approval without a photo, it does not confirm that signs were actually mounted facing the paths on opening day."}

parsed.note: Claim C is supported by the signed carrier slip in S1 confirming Thursday delivery. Claim B is contradicted by S2, which lists four aluminium signs, indicating the signs were not made of wood. Claim A is unresolved; while S3 describes intended orientation and approval without a photo, it does not confirm that signs were actually mounted facing the paths on opening day.
